dialogue.user: Thanks for these suggestions! Could you tell me a bit more about "Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World"? Specifically, what do reviewers say about it?
dialogue.agent:
"Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World" is $12.99, has a 5.0-star average rating, and 3 reviews. It’s both inspirational and practical, helping families plan and embrace world travel with children. It covers logistics, schooling, remote work, and includes personal stories from families who have done it.

According to reviewers:
- They appreciate its unique mix of inspiration and practical advice, especially for parents looking for alternatives to traditional schooling.
- Readers found the author’s real-life stories about traveling families motivational and helpful, highlighting how travel can benefit both children and parents.
- One reviewer noted the book encourages reflection and shows travel can be affordable and enriching, helping families find community and manage challenges on the road.

Would you like to know anything else or explore similar books?

result.title: Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World
result.features: You don’t have to decide whether to work OR travel...you can do both! Hit the Road! is a book to inspire families who have always dreamed of traveling with their children. Whether for a year or a lifetime, if you’re a single mother of one or a traditional family of five, this book explains how to take those first steps to get on the road, and what to do once you’re there. It looks at logistics and schooling, remote working, and how to meet others, travel emergencies, and much more.Filled with inspiration, practical information, and personal anecdotes – interviews with traveling families who share how they did it and their lessons learned – Hit the Road! will educate you about the fast-growing community of “Worldschooling” and traveling families. If you are someone who marvels at other families traveling the world and imagine doing the same, then this book is for you! So many families are already doing it... you can too.

top_reviews.title: For the thoughtful and adventurous parents
top_reviews.text:
If you have ever felt constricted by the American cultural paradigms of education for your children, then this book is for you. Ms Pollon takes you through a teaching of reflection upon how to affordably optimize your parenting years for you and your child. The book explains so many different ways to educate our children. The many stories of families that have had positive experiences through travel are refreshingly presented.
Be sure to reflect on the journaling exercises- the results are worth the effort.
This book is a powerful reminder that we have choices in how to educate our children and still care for ourselves as parents.
For those who want to raise a citizen of this world- read and reflect upon this book.

top_reviews.title: Worldschooling FTW!!
top_reviews.text:
Zelie is such an inspiration and it's fantastic that she has put so many of her lessons and experiences together in this book for other families to see that it really is possible! We first met back in 2018 in Guanajuato, Mexico at a gathering for traveling families. At that time our family were new to the "world is my classroom" concept, but Zelie showed us what is possible and some pitfalls to avoid. We went on to travel to India, Thailand, Italy and Kenya. Both my kids turned out amazing and my son now is applying to the top universities in the world.

You can do it too! Zelie can show you how.

top_reviews.title: A wonderful, unique guide for families
top_reviews.text:
This book is one-of-kind among travel books. It is both a practical and an inspirational guide for people and especially families who want to travel--not just to "see the sights" but to get to know new people and places on a deeper level, and for a longer time. It's a book for people who are open and willing to be changed by their experiences, and to allow their children to gain perspectives that aren't readily available in their media-saturated, consumerist world. She tells stories of cultures that deeply love and value children; of the growing number of people making a living working remotely; of finding satisfaction with fewer material things, of wealth measured in friendship and experiences rather than dollars; of children who learn languages and skills not available to them at home and come into adulthood with real intellectual and social advantages and unusual maturity.
The book is filled with practical advice so you can avoid the mistakes of first-time world travelers, and can stay safe and secure in new environments. Above all it's filled with a sense of possibility and adventure, and shows that no matter what your circumstances you don't have to stay in your rut, waiting for some perfect future time to get on the road--and you don't need to be wealthy (in fact many actually do better financially living abroad). And when you do decide to get up and go, you'll be surrounded by other like-minded people from your country and from all over the world with whom to find support and share your adventures!
